difficulty.reason: Two distinct verification paths: Sensitive scopes require written justification for each scope, an Unlisted YouTube demo video showing client ID visible in the address bar, and Search Console domain verification (Google says it can take up to 10 days, and no security assessment is required). Restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/) require all of that plus an annual security assessment by a Google-approved assessor at least every 12 months (Google says can take several weeks; 2 to 6 weeks is an unverified estimate).

timeEstimate.approvalWait: Sensitive: up to 10 days; Restricted: several weeks (2 to 6 weeks)
timeEstimate.notes: Sensitive scopes: verification takes up to 10 days (no security assessment required). Restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/): Google says verification can take several weeks, with 2 to 6 weeks being an unverified estimate depending on third-party assessor turnaround.

requirements.text: The homepage must be public and describe the app
The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage
Each sensitive scope needs a written justification
Domain verified in Search Console by a project Owner or Editor
Unlisted YouTube demo video showing client ID visible in the address bar and demonstrating how the app uses requested scopes
Annual reassessment (at least every 12 months) by a Google approved assessor for restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/)
CASA Tier 2 security assessment for restricted scopes
$500 to $3,000 dollar fee paid to third-party security lab for restricted scope assessment
Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project with billing enabled
Up to 100 test users allowed in OAuth consent screen testing mode before verification

steps.title: Create a GCP Project & Enable APIs
steps.description: Go to Google Cloud Console, create a new project, and enable the target APIs (such as Gmail API for full Gmail access) in the API Library.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen, Homepage & Privacy Policy
steps.description: Select User Type 'External'. Enter App Name, Support Email, and Developer Email. The homepage must be public and describe the app, and the privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage.

steps.title: Domain Verification in Search Console by Owner or Editor
steps.description: Verify your domain ownership in Google Search Console. The domain must be verified by a user who is designated as an Owner or Editor on the Google Cloud project.

steps.title: Record Unlisted YouTube Demo Video
steps.description: Record an Unlisted YouTube demo video showing: 1) the OAuth grant consent screen with client ID visible in the address bar, and 2) how your app uses requested scopes in user interface features.

steps.title: Submit Sensitive Scopes: Written Justifications
steps.description: Case 1 (Sensitive Scopes): Submit for verification in GCP Console. Each sensitive scope needs a written justification explaining why non-sensitive scopes are inadequate. Google says it can take up to 10 days, and no security assessment is required.

steps.title: Submit Restricted Scopes: Annual Security Assessment
steps.description: Case 2 (Restricted Scopes, such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/): Requires all sensitive scope items plus an annual security assessment by a Google approved assessor (at least every 12 months). Google says it can take several weeks (2 to 6 weeks is an unverified estimate; community reports CASA Tier 2 fees of $500 to $3,000).

blockers.problem: Verification rejected due to homepage or privacy policy domain mismatch
blockers.solution: Ensure the homepage is public and describes the app, and the privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage. Domain must be verified in Search Console by a project Owner or Editor.

blockers.problem: Demo video rejected because client ID is not visible in address bar or video is not Unlisted
blockers.solution: Re-record an Unlisted YouTube demo video ensuring the browser address bar clearly shows the full `client_id` query parameter during the OAuth redirect, and demonstrating how the app uses requested scopes.

blockers.problem: Sensitive scope rejected for inadequate written justification
blockers.solution: Each sensitive scope needs a written justification explaining user-facing necessity. Sensitive scopes do not require a security assessment (Google says review takes up to 10 days).

blockers.problem: Restricted scope security assessment costs ($500 to $3,000) and lead times (several weeks / 2 to 6 weeks)
blockers.solution: Restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/) require all sensitive scope criteria plus an annual security assessment by a Google approved assessor at least every 12 months. Google says it can take several weeks (2 to 6 weeks unverified estimate; community reports CASA Tier 2 fees of $500 to $3,000). Sensitive scopes do not require a security assessment.

managedOption.managedSufficientWhen: Composio's pre-verified Google OAuth app is the fastest path when building AI assistants or agent tools that need restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/) without spending several weeks (2 to 6 weeks unverified estimate) and $500 to $3,000 on annual security assessments. This tool was built for a Composio assignment, and Composio sells managed OAuth.
managedOption.customRequiredWhen: You must complete custom Google verification if your enterprise customers demand your specific brand name on the Google consent dialog, or if your enterprise security policy prohibits routing tokens through a third-party managed infrastructure.

claims.claim: Sensitive scopes: verification needs a justification for each scope, an Unlisted YouTube demo video with client ID visible in the address bar, and domain verification in Search Console by a project Owner or Editor. Google says it can take up to 10 days, and no security assessment is required.

Restricted scopes (such as full Gmail access: https://mail.google.com/): all sensitive scope requirements plus an annual security assessment by a Google approved assessor (at least every 12 months), which Google says can take several weeks.
Google OAuth app approval and security assessment for restricted scopes takes 2 to 6 weeks.
Restricted scopes require a CASA Tier 2 security assessment with third-party assessor fees ranging from $500 to $3,000.
The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage, and the homepage must be public and describe the app.
Creating and verifying an OAuth app requires a GCP project with billing enabled and allows up to 100 test users before submission.
